HOME.faq.demo_a: Yes. We run demonstrations — get in touch and we will arrange one.
HOME.faq.demo_q: Can we see one working first?
HOME.faq.heading: Questions we get asked
HOME.faq.layout_a: The L3 and SP50 update their floor maps automatically, so a changed layout does not need a new survey.
HOME.faq.layout_q: What happens when we move shelving or change the layout?
HOME.faq.operate_a: No. Routes are mapped once at deployment, after which the machine runs to schedule and docks itself when it finishes. Anyone on shift can start it, stop it or return it to the dock from the onboard touchscreen, without specialist training.
HOME.faq.operate_q: Does someone need to operate it?
HOME.faq.runtime_a: Between three and six hours of continuous work depending on the model, recharging in one and a half to four hours. The SP50 patrols for up to 13 hours. Several models dock and recharge themselves between runs.
HOME.faq.runtime_q: How long does it run before charging?
HOME.faq.safety_a: The machines detect obstacles at up to 150 m, including protruding objects and the floor-to-ceiling glass that defeats simpler sensors. The S5 additionally recognises forklifts and AGVs and keeps clear of them.
HOME.faq.safety_q: Is it safe around staff, customers and vehicles?
HOME.faq.staff_a: In practice it changes what they spend their time on. Aspirus Hospital reported that their team moved onto deep scrubbing, stripping and waxing once the robots took over routine floor coverage — the work that needs judgement, rather than the work that needs repetition.
HOME.faq.staff_q: Does this replace our cleaning staff?
HOME.faq.support_a: Yes. We respond within 24 hours, hold spare parts, and carry out the maintenance ourselves.
HOME.faq.support_q: Do you service and support these in Thailand?
HOME.faq.tops_a: TOPS stands for trillion operations per second — a measure of how much AI processing the robot's onboard chip can do. On a cleaning machine that capacity goes on reading the LiDAR and cameras many times a second: spotting obstacles, planning a route, and recognising what is on the floor. More TOPS means the machine can run heavier perception models and react faster in a busy space. The L3 and S5 carry 100 TOPS of NVIDIA compute; the L4 carries 32 TOPS.
HOME.faq.tops_q: What does "100 TOPS AI compute" mean?
HOME.faq.which_a: It depends on the floor rather than the building. The L3 passes through 700 mm gaps, for tight retail, hospitals and schools. The L4 clears a standard doorway at 810 mm and scrubs to within 3 cm of the wall. The L50 is built for warehouse-scale open floor. The S5 sweeps dry debris in industrial settings. The SP50 patrols for scattered mess instead of scrubbing everything. Tell us the size, floor type and operating hours and we will recommend one.
HOME.faq.which_q: Which of the five machines do we need?

ROBOT.c5.f1.body: Dual side brushes pull debris in from the edges, the roller brush and 25 kg of scrubbing pressure take the floor down to clean, and the dust mop finishes behind. Heavily soiled floors come back in a single pass instead of three.
ROBOT.c5.f1.bullet1: Sweeping, scrubbing and dust mopping combined
ROBOT.c5.f1.title: Sweep, scrub and mop — in one run
ROBOT.c5.f2.body: Laser-vision fusion positioning keeps the C5 located when either sensor alone would drift — through glass atriums, past mirrored shopfronts, across the wide open floors that defeat pure-LiDAR machines.
ROBOT.c5.f2.title: Laser and vision, fused
ROBOT.c5.f3.body: The dirtiest job on any scrubber is the sewage tank, and it is the one people skip. The C5 flushes its own in four minutes at the workstation — then refills, charges and goes back out.
ROBOT.c5.f3.bullet3: Closed-loop cleaning re-covers any missed area
ROBOT.c5.f3.title: It cleans its own tank
ROBOT.c5.f4.body: Start a job from the robot's own screen, dispatch it from your phone, or schedule the whole week from the cloud console — with job reports waiting for you either way.
ROBOT.c5.f4.bullet1: Triple-platform control: robot, mobile and cloud
ROBOT.c5.f4.bullet2: Autonomous boundary recognition and map updates
ROBOT.c5.f4.title: On the machine, on your phone, in the cloud
ROBOT.c5.f5.body: A compact station that fills at up to 10 litres a minute, drains at up to 15, and runs the tank self-clean cycle. Where there is no plumbing, a mobile tank configuration does the same job.
ROBOT.c5.f5.bullet1: Automatic fill, drain and sewage self-clean
ROBOT.c5.f5.bullet2: 8 L onboard tank, 1,800 W peak draw
ROBOT.c5.f5.bullet3: Mobile tank option for sites without plumbing
ROBOT.c5.f5.title: The dock does the dirty work
ROBOT.c5.highlight1: Sweeps, scrubs and mops in one pass
ROBOT.c5.highlight2: 90 L tank — largest in the fleet
ROBOT.c5.intro: Most floors need three machines and three passes. The C5 needs one. It sweeps debris, scrubs the floor and dust mops behind itself in a single run, carries 90 litres of water to do it, and returns to a workstation that refills, drains and flushes its own sewage tank in four minutes.
ROBOT.c5.pickif: Your floors need sweeping, scrubbing and mopping, and running three separate machines over the same ground is not practical.
ROBOT.c5.pitch: Sweeps, scrubs and dust mops in a single pass — with a 90-litre tank and a workstation that refills and cleans itself.
ROBOT.l3.f1.body: NVIDIA silicon rated at 100 TOPS reads a 96-beam 3D LiDAR point cloud in real time. The L3 doesn't follow a painted line — it builds a live map, plans its own routes, and re-plans the moment a pallet, bed or person appears where the map says floor.
ROBOT.l3.f1.bullet1: Autonomous path planning with live re-routing
ROBOT.l3.f1.bullet2: Obstacle avoidance tuned for occupied buildings
ROBOT.l3.f1.bullet3: Maps update themselves when your layout changes
ROBOT.l3.f1.title: A supercomputer pushing a scrubber
ROBOT.l3.f2.body: Ground-level perception detects the things that stop other robots and hurt staff — temporary carpets, loose cables, mats at a wet entrance. The L3 classifies them and cleans around them instead of eating them.
ROBOT.l3.f2.bullet2: Safe behaviour around doors and entrances
ROBOT.l3.f2.bullet3: Designed for daytime operation among people
ROBOT.l3.f2.title: Sees the hazards people trip on
ROBOT.l3.f3.body: Simple voice commands start, pause and redirect the robot — no gloves off, no screen taps. For clinical environments where hands stay clean, that's not a gimmick; it's infection control.
ROBOT.l3.f3.bullet2: Full mobile app for routes, alerts and reports
ROBOT.l3.f3.title: Tell it. Don't touch it.
ROBOT.l3.f4.body: A large-access recovery tank, magnetic quick-swap brushes and a quick-release squeegee mean the daily service routine doesn't need a technician — or a coffee break.
ROBOT.l3.f4.bullet1: Magnetic brushes drop in and out by hand
ROBOT.l3.f4.bullet3: Wide-mouth recovery tank for fast rinse-out
ROBOT.l3.f4.title: Maintenance measured in seconds
ROBOT.l3.f5.body: Pair the L3 with the WS3 workstation and WT3 mobile water tank (60 L fresh / 50 L recovery) and it runs extended cleaning cycles in buildings with no fixed water connection at all.
ROBOT.l3.f5.bullet2: WT3 mobile tank: 60 L fresh, 50 L recovery
ROBOT.l3.f5.bullet3: Off-hours cycles without a water hookup
ROBOT.l3.f5.title: No plumbing? No problem.
ROBOT.l3.intro: The L3 carries a 100 TOPS NVIDIA AI platform and a 96-beam 3D LiDAR in a body narrow enough for a hospital corridor at visiting hours. It plans its own routes, avoids what people leave in them, and answers to plain voice commands.
ROBOT.l3.pickif: Your floors have narrow corridors, standard doorways or crowded aisles where a larger machine simply cannot fit — hospital wings, classrooms, small-format retail.
ROBOT.l3.pitch: Compact AI floor scrubber that passes through 700 mm gaps — built for hospitals, schools and tight retail floors.
ROBOT.l4.f1.body: Vision AI classifies stains in its path and adjusts brush pressure, water flow and speed on the spot — full effort on the spill, light touch on the clean run.
ROBOT.l4.f1.bullet2: Automatic pressure, flow and speed adjustment
ROBOT.l4.f1.bullet3: Solution flow tracks cleaning speed to cut waste
ROBOT.l4.f1.title: Cleans harder where it's dirtier
ROBOT.l4.f2.body: Most rivals in this class can't pass a standard door frame. The L4 does — then hugs walls and shelving to under 3 cm, where the dirt actually collects.
ROBOT.l4.f2.bullet1: 810 mm passage width clears standard doorways
ROBOT.l4.f2.bullet2: Edge distance under 3 cm along walls and racking
ROBOT.l4.f2.bullet3: 1,100 mm turning width for tight aisle ends
ROBOT.l4.f2.title: Through the doorway, along the edge
ROBOT.l4.f3.body: A 32-beam 3D LiDAR with 150 m of range, backed by 3D depth cameras and bumper sensors, maps the building and everything moving through it — so the L4 plans clean lines and gives people and pallet trucks a wide berth.
ROBOT.l4.f3.bullet3: Re-plans live when the aisle changes
ROBOT.l4.f3.title: A 150-metre head start
ROBOT.l4.f4.body: Every run ends with a report: route map, coverage percentage, area cleaned, water and detergent used, minutes worked. Plan routes, get completion alerts, and prove the clean happened — without walking the floor.
ROBOT.l4.f4.bullet2: Coverage and consumption reports per run
ROBOT.l4.f4.bullet3: Completion and fault alerts to your phone
ROBOT.l4.f4.title: The whole night, reported
ROBOT.l4.f5.body: Docked at its workstation the L4 empties, refills, charges and returns to work without a human in the loop. Squeegee replacement takes 30 seconds when it's finally due.
ROBOT.l4.f5.bullet1: Autonomous empty, refill and charge cycles
ROBOT.l4.f5.bullet2: Overnight cleaning with nobody on site
ROBOT.l4.f5.title: The 4-in-1 workstation
ROBOT.l4.highlight2: Scrubs to 3 cm from the wall
ROBOT.l4.intro: At 810 mm passage width the L4 goes through a standard door frame, then cleans to within 3 cm of the skirting board. Stain-perception AI adjusts water, pressure and speed to what it actually sees on the floor.
ROBOT.l4.pickif: You clean occupied retail floors or hotel public areas during trading hours, and need the edges and skirting done properly, not just the middle.
ROBOT.l4.pitch: The volume workhorse for retail and hospitality — fits a standard doorway and scrubs to within 3 cm of the wall.
ROBOT.l50.f1.body: The 120 Ah battery and 55-litre tank are sized so one dispatch covers 3,700–5,600 square metres — a full night's floor in most facilities — before it needs water or power.
ROBOT.l50.f1.bullet1: Up to 6 hours on one charge
ROBOT.l50.f1.bullet2: 55 L solution tank, 25 kg brush pressure
ROBOT.l50.f1.bullet3: Built for epoxy and sealed concrete floors
ROBOT.l50.f1.title: A full shift without a refill
ROBOT.l50.f2.body: Long-range LiDAR plus protruding-object and glass detection keep it safe among racking, forklifts and floor-to-ceiling storefronts — the hazards that blind lesser machines.
ROBOT.l50.f2.title: Sees 150 metres down the aisle
ROBOT.l50.f3.body: The onboard touchscreen shows task progress, schedules and alarms, with one-touch pause, stop and dispatch. Anyone on the night crew can drive the whole operation without training.
ROBOT.l50.f3.title: Mission control, on the machine
ROBOT.l50.f4.body: Plan routes, watch live location, and get completion reports with coverage and consumption per run. Over-the-air updates add capability while the robot sleeps.
ROBOT.l50.f4.title: Not a speck missed
ROBOT.l50.f5.body: The CWS workstation lets the L50 swap its own water — discharging the recovery tank and refilling solution against docking fiducials, then heading straight back to the floor.
ROBOT.l50.f5.title: Docks. Drains. Refills. Returns.
ROBOT.l50.intro: Built for warehouses, logistics hubs and big-box floors: a 55-litre solution tank, 25 kg of brush pressure for epoxy floors, and a battery that runs a full shift. It covers 3,700–5,600 square metres on a single charge without asking for anything.
ROBOT.l50.pickif: You have large open floors where the machine spends more time going back for water than cleaning — distribution centres, big-box retail, industrial units.
ROBOT.l50.pitch: The warehouse workhorse — 55 L tank, 6-hour runtime, and 3,700–5,600 m² covered without a refill.
ROBOT.s5.f1.body: S5 units coordinate as a fleet, dividing the floor between them and adapting when one is charging. Big facilities clean in a fraction of the time.
ROBOT.s5.f1.title: One floor, many sweepers
ROBOT.s5.f2.body: Purpose-trained recognition for forklifts, AGVs and site vehicles means the S5 yields early and keeps working around live traffic, not just after hours.
ROBOT.s5.f2.title: Knows a forklift when it sees one
ROBOT.s5.f3.body: Advanced dust control plus a 50-litre hopper handles fine powder and coarse industrial waste in the same pass — film, cardboard, screws, bottle caps.
ROBOT.s5.f3.title: From dust to dropped bolts
ROBOT.s5.f4.body: The hopper lifts out without tools, filters shake clean in seconds, and every wear part is reachable from the outside — service fits inside a coffee break, not a maintenance window.
ROBOT.s5.f4.title: Empty it and go
ROBOT.s5.f5.body: A 2-hour fast charge and its own docking station keep the S5 in rotation — it tops up between shifts and returns to its route without being asked.
ROBOT.s5.f5.title: Charges in two hours, works around the clock
ROBOT.s5.intro: From fine dust to wood chips, packaging film, bottles and screws — the S5 sweeps the dry side of industrial floors at 2,500 m²/h. TeamClean lets several units carve up a warehouse together, and vehicle recognition keeps them clear of your forklifts.
ROBOT.s5.pickif: Your mess is dry — dust, packaging film, offcuts, bottle caps — on floors where you do not want water at all.
ROBOT.s5.pitch: AI-driven industrial sweeper for dry debris — 2,500 m²/h, and it works in coordinated fleets.
ROBOT.sp50.f1.body: Because it cleans only where its AI sees dirt, the SP50 patrols roughly eight times the area of a full-coverage machine — the right shape for food courts, terminals and lobbies where mess is constant but scattered.
ROBOT.sp50.f1.bullet1: 15,550 m²/h patrolling versus 1,987 m²/h full coverage
ROBOT.sp50.f1.bullet2: Cleans on detection, not on a fixed route
ROBOT.sp50.f1.bullet3: Automatic map updates when the floor plan changes
ROBOT.sp50.f1.title: Eight times the ground, same shift
ROBOT.sp50.f2.body: The onboard model identifies waste types with 99% accuracy — dropped fries, spilt drinks, shredded paper — and picks the approach each one needs rather than treating every mark the same.
ROBOT.sp50.f2.bullet3: 25 kPa suction applied where it counts
ROBOT.sp50.f2.title: A ten-billion-parameter eye for mess
ROBOT.sp50.f3.body: The onboard touchscreen shows task progress, schedules and alarms, with one-touch continue, stop and return-to-dock. Anyone on shift can drive it without training.
ROBOT.sp50.f3.title: Run it from the machine
ROBOT.sp50.f4.body: 150 metres of detection range, plus protruding-object and glass detection, keep the SP50 safe in crowds and against the floor-to-ceiling glass that defeats lesser machines. Edge cleaning reaches within 5 cm of the wall.
ROBOT.sp50.f4.title: Built to work among people
ROBOT.sp50.f5.body: The CCS-02 workstation takes the machine back between patrols — charging it and handling the debris so the 18-litre filter bag and 5-litre tray last far longer than a shift.
ROBOT.sp50.f5.bullet2: 18 L dust filter bag, 5 L trash tray
ROBOT.sp50.f5.title: Empties and charges itself
ROBOT.sp50.f6.body: A live retail concourse — glass frontage, seating, foot traffic that never quite stops. This is the floor the SP50 is built for: it patrols for what has actually been dropped, rather than working a fixed route across every square metre of it.
ROBOT.sp50.f6.title: A floor that is still in use
ROBOT.sp50.highlight1: Cleans only where the mess is
ROBOT.sp50.highlight3: Up to 13 hours on one charge
ROBOT.sp50.intro: Full-coverage cleaning spends most of its effort on floor that was already clean. The SP50 patrols instead: a 10-billion-parameter model recognises debris with 99% accuracy, and 25 kPa of suction goes exactly where it is needed. The result is up to 15,550 square metres an hour — roughly eight times what the same machine manages scrubbing every inch.
ROBOT.sp50.pickif: Your floors are broadly clean but constantly picking up scattered mess — dropped food, spills, litter — across an area far too large to keep scrubbing end to end.
ROBOT.sp50.pitch: Patrols for spills and litter instead of scrubbing everything — covering up to 15,550 m²/h because it only stops where there is something to clean.
ROBOT.sp50.tagline: Finds the mess. Skips the rest.
